claims.statement: Poland's deposit-return system has operated since 1 October 2025 and adds a refundable deposit to covered beverage packaging.
Official guidance says the deposit follows the package through the sales chain and beverage producers placing covered packages on the market finance the system.
Polish climate-ministry guidance states that stores above 200 square metres must accept marked containers, creating recurring multi-location return records.

contrary_evidence: Deposit-system operators and reverse-vending vendors are incentivized to provide their own reconciliation portals.
The system's early transition noise may decline, reducing recoverable discrepancies after operational maturation.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot a 20-50-store regional group, quantify leakage, then distribute through one POS vendor or beverage wholesaler on revenue share
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1,200 stores at 400 PLN monthly creates 5.76m PLN ARR by years 4-6. With partner-led support, 20%+ operating margin and majority ownership, retained cash plus a 4-5x valuation could cross 5m PLN founder net worth in years 5-7.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly; field visits can be delegated after one direct observation cycle
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 78-90% once mappings are reusable; initial operator/POS mappings and manual evidence cleanup lower first-year margin
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 3-6 months through a channel-led chain rollout; single-store acquisition is uneconomic
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 250-750 PLN per store monthly, 3,000-15,000 PLN chain onboarding, and optionally 8-15% of documented recoveries
economics.retention_or_repeat: Deposits and returns settle continuously; historical store/operator baselines improve anomaly detection and make monthly close habitual

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-operator discrepancy taxonomy, store-level expected-return models and evidence templates improve recovery rates and reveal systematic leakage
fingerprint.customer: Polish convenience chains, franchise groups, forecourt retailers and beverage wholesalers handling marked deposit containers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Integrate through regional POS vendors, RVM service firms and beverage wholesalers that can roll the tool across hundreds of merchant locations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Per-store SaaS plus optional success fee on recovered discrepancies, with white-label portfolio views for POS vendors and wholesalers
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Retail group pays per active store when the monthly deposit close and discrepancy claims are produced; onboarding is paid per POS/operator connection
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Container sales, returns, pickups and an operator's settlement statement do not balance by store, SKU, day or operator

founder_fit: Anomaly detection and multi-source matching fit the founder's analytical strengths.
A regional pilot can start within 100,000 PLN and alongside employment.
risks: A low per-store price cannot support bespoke integrations or field service.
Operator statement formats and commercial contracts may restrict data portability.
Success fees must be structured as accounting recovery, not unauthorized legal representation.

structure.control_point: Retailer's approval of deposit-system operator statements and settlement invoices
structure.critical_dependency: Machine-readable store, return-machine, pickup and operator statement data plus willingness of channel partners to support a neutral layer

thesis: Build a neutral reconciliation layer for Polish convenience chains, franchise groups and beverage wholesalers that operate across deposit-system operators. It matches POS deposits charged, manual or reverse-vending returns, pickup counts, operator statements, invoices and bank settlements, then routes discrepancies to the responsible operator with a compact evidence packet. Start as a monthly recovery audit for one retail group and become embedded middleware through POS and beverage-wholesaler channels. The business never holds consumer deposits; it reconciles the retailer's records.
title: Deposit-Return Settlement Switchboard
uncertainties: Observed discrepancy value per store per month
Number of operators a typical regional chain must reconcile
POS and RVM export quality outside large chains
